_sources.record: Head counts, dates, and the lesson and video counts come from the course's own files.
_sources.ladder: The course document: eleven tiers, belt names and themes as written.
_sources.intensive: What happened, not what was planned. Blocks and their order come from the index of the session recordings and from Andrew's own run sheet for his slots. 'mine' marks only blocks where the recordings show him presenting: Session 1 clip 17 (the rap's prompt walkthrough), clips 18 and 19 (the Skill plenary and its live demo), and Session 2 clip 08 (the capstone kickoff). Blocks that come only from his run sheet carry 'runSheet' and say so on the page: the Day 2 job search panel and polish-and-ship are in no recording. 'watch' links a block to a published recording of it, with its length; '#clip' means the clip on the same page. The Skill plenary is not published, so it has no link. The planning document is not used.
_sources.capstone: The course's standard for the top rung.
_sources.brief: Each block's 'brief' is one clause cut from its own 'what' for the run sheet. It adds nothing that 'what' does not say.
_sources.notes: Clock times are left out: the schedule drafts disagree about them, and the recordings are cut, so clip lengths are not block lengths. Per-rung lesson counts are left out because the files disagree. No instructor, guest or attendee is named.

said.setup: Setup happened in the room on Day 1: after the opening talks, everyone installed Claude Code and had Claude interview them to write a context file.
said.skill: In my plenary I showed the resume-tailoring Skill I use myself, live in my own terminal, and gave the room the same build: have Claude interview you into one long master resume, pick an output format, and save that format as a Skill.
said.agents: Sub-agents and agent fleets were shown on Day 1 as a preview, and the hands-on build stayed with one agent.
said.capstone: For the capstone, people picked a real task, had Claude make mock data, and started building that evening in plan mode.

blocks.name: Welcome and intros

blocks.what: Why Claude Dojo, a poll of the room, the instructors, and the plan for both days.

blocks.name: What changed in AI

blocks.what: Hands-on: connecting the Canva MCP server to Claude, so it can reach an app outside the terminal.
